To begin with, I will start by saying that I will only be discussing the base game (Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn) and the subsequently related patches (2.0 through 2.55) only. If you are interested in reading further about the game beyond the base: please read my reviews for Heavensward and Stormblood on the respective store pages.
The whole mythos surrounding this game is legendary and truly deserves applause and commendation for resurrecting a game that nearly bankrupted SquareEnix because of a disastrous launch, poor design decisions, abysmal technical implementation, and delusional management that were in denial about the true state of the game. The result, being a cumulative three year project to overhaul the game, was Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn. As a veteran of the first version of the game (1.0), SquareEnix, mainly the production team, took all of the player's concerns and complaints to heart and really overhauled the entire system and the work shows.
The story is slow to start with everything starting from approximately level 1 upwards to level 30 being a tiered tutorial to immerse you into the many intricate systems of crafting, gathering, fighting, jobs, dungeons, raids, bosses, grand companies, free companies, and so much more. When the game sets you free at level 15, you truly have the whole world to explore and complete freedom of choice to do whatever you please. Your chocobo, assigned to you through your grand company of choice (think of a grand company as a governmental body's military), will become your closest ally and a partner in battle.
At the time of the writing, classes are still implemented into the game as it is but with SquareEnix announcing that in the next expansion after Stormblood, they will be completely removed for a completely job oriented system. The battle system as been revamped as well with skills, abilities, and cross-class abilities being merged, moved, and removed from the game has forced the entire population to learn a new dynamic.
SquareEnix also is runs a mentor system which puts you into a linkshell (a sort of group chat) with other mentors and novices so that any questions you have can be immediately answered by experienced players who can provide you with solid information. There is also a crown next to those with little insignia to identify what they're a mentor of. To be warned, the novice network can both be positive and toxic depending on your server, with some worse than others. Do not be afraid to leave the novice network and instead seek out a free company (a guild in most other games) for guidance and help learning the game- that is a much more stable and positive experience.
The graphics are beautiful with the game currently running on DirectX 11 with plans to move it to DirectX 12 in the future. It runs well on weaker systems but has enough versatility to really push your system to the limits on the ultra graphics setting. I'd expect nothing less from a Final Fantasy MMO. Be warned, MMORPGs are CPU intensive so even with a great graphics card, if your processor isn't up to snuff, you're going to have a tough time handling much larger world events such as hunts or FATEs (Full-Action Timed Event) that spawn world bosses such as Odin and Behemoth.
Palace of the Dead, FATEs, and Dungeons will be your primary way of leveling with side-quests and the main scenario quests being your bread and butter. It isn't entirely rare for you to outlevel the content that you're going through- just grab another job and begin leveling it up in the process. This freedom to not be tied to a single job makes Final Fantasy XIV riskless in terms of role investment. Gaining levels is a non-issue in the game with so many incentives and systems in place to get you to the current expansion in place, you're going to be more focused on being properly geared for content over actually getting to it.
The story is slow to begin with and then quickly picks up around 35 to 45. Things really escalate quickly in your post-50 content where your main scenario is bridging the story between A Realm Reborn and Heavensward. In my opinion, this is where the storytelling that this franchise has come to know truly shines and isn't afraid to be brutal, honest, and emotional. Any game that gets me emotionally involved with characters and attached to them is definitely a winner in my books. Overall, the story is approximately over 100 hours long and the music is nothing short of impressive for a MMO. In fact, A Realm Reborn contains over 100 individual tracks of music written by Nobou Uematsu and Masayoshi Soken, truly make this feel like a well developed game and darn close to being less MMO and more CO-OP.
I'd highly recommend this game for people hopping MMOs, looking to get into one, or someone looking for a solid entry into the Final Fantasy XIV franchise I cannot recommend this game enough to you.

Essentially an economy/trading sim built on an intergalactic platform, Endless Sky will, repeat, will devour your time. Building your ships and fleets becomes an obsession, and you find yourself spending a fair amount of time trying to maximixe profits by finding the most lucrative trade routes and missions.
... and then you throw in the pirate attacks, warring factions, and underlying story....
Would definitely recommend this one to anyboby beyond the 'casual gamer,' who may find the pace and depth of detail boring.
Otherwise, you can't beat it for the price!

A very good game in the Men of War engine with a few issues. Most notably:
-difficulty is all over the place. For example, the first Russian mission has you sabotaging some trains guarded by about 200 Germans with a total of less than a dozen men. The second mission has you defending a town with hundreds of men and artillery against Germans who basically walk across a field at you.
-field artillery is laser accurate and extremely deadly. This can either be a bit comical or extremely annoying depending on the mission
-the voice acting is really bizzare at times
Despite what many negative reviews say, these things are far from game-ruining. The devs clearly aren't professionals with a great deal of resources and these issues reflect that. However, the solid experience far outweighs these cons in my opinion.

Yes the game has some rough spots, but I  enjoy it for the most part. ESPECIALLY the editor, I've spent countless hours recreating famous ww1 battles/scenarios, gets pretty addicting. The campaign suffers from difficulty/ slight bugs, and horrendous voice acting. However, I still find joy in it, especially since most nations are playable. (Give us Italy please).
Overall, 7/10.

Factorio. Really jewel on current market of pc games. Unique. Intriguing and solid. Both in game and in its marketing.
Keeping its price same for years, never yielding into temptation of "steam sale" or anything, steadily developing and polishing for long time even though base game from start to end was done years ago and many less scrupulous developers would try and release it for some quick cash.
On top of that offering Demo version which is very welcomed and rare nowadays.
Every other game developer should take this game as example how to do things corectly.
As for game itself...
Posibilities are endless and there is something for everyone.
For those who are less technicaly inclined it is reasonably easy to simply go for Rocket Launch while enjoying fruits of their labors, watching how that extremely expensive rocket is being build by itself thanks to their time spent on automatization of everything.
But for those who love to get to the crux... depth of this game, especialy with mods, is insane. Kudos to developers who managed to integrate logicstic programing into game and make it fun.

This game is just ridiculous. There is not much complexity with the graphics as it looks like the first Starcraft with the 16 bit sprites and all. However that is the only con I'll probably write about in this review. Factorio is a simulation/building/realtime strategy game that draws you in with it's glamorous at first micromanagement, to the later on autonomous creating robot phase. The first playthrough I didn't get to the robots and I thought, hey... I'm having to do alot of manual labor here! The 2nd playthrough I had changed my strategy and started planning out my resource belts going to the forge making area, then those belts going to the productions lines, then those belts transporting to storage for later use items, and then those going to my future rail line power production area, and then those belts going to... Get the point?
If you are the type of gamer who likes building simulations or micro management style games, this is the game for you. This game may not be for you if you have to have story or a goal driving you forward throughout the game. There is a campaign mode which assigns goals and I have played through the first 5 scenarios. Mainly just to get the hang of the basics. I will wait to play the whole campaign when the game is released in it's final form. Currently I've been playing in Sandbox mode. In this game you make up your own goals which become infinite over time because yes you guessed it... The map is an infinite procedural generated map with an unlimited area to develop with varying resources spread throughout. Enemies are present depending on how dense you set them in the map creation screen. You do have to set up defenses as these alien life forms do not like the pollution your machines are creating. Later on you can develop weapons and go on the offensive to wipe them out to prevent future attacks. Until you expand your factory to another area that is...
Well enough rambling already! I've got to get my renewable solar energy powerplant blueprint going so I can assign my robots to expand upon my power grid! As my oil supply can't keep up and my local coal source is dwindling, I guess I should ask myself: Is it really 3am and do I have to go to work tomorrow?

I don't review much, and I typically am not an MMO fan.  To date, the only ones I've put significant time towards are DC Universe Online and Star Trek Online.  However, after logging 86.8 hours of FFXIV in a bit under 10 days, despite being a gainfully employed adult, I'd have to give this one an overwhelmingly positive review.
This is the first FF game in a long while (probably since FF7 - which I played when it originally came out), that has made me not want to tear myself away from playing.  The story/dialogue can be a little cheesy sometimes, but it's FF, it's supposed to be.
Game mechanics are fun, can be learned easily, and with the XP boost until lvl 60, it gives noobs an easy opportunity to try different classes (or all of them) without it being particularly punishing if you don't like one.  The game does a great job of drawing you in an letting you try being anything you want easily.
People that tend to lean towards soloing can have plenty of fun (I tend this direction), and as far as I've seen the community is predominantly kind and willing to teach.  You can also easily find groups (Free Companies - which are equal to Guilds, Leagues, Fleets, etc. in other MMOs) to join and they are eager to help you learn the ropes.
There's plenty to do and try in FFXIV and fun to be had.  It's consistently rated in the top MMOs for good reason.
The only negative aspect I see is that it is a subscription based model, but there's an indefinite free trial now.  So, you can experience everything up to level 35 with all of the classes before you decide if you're willing to give SE your money.

Fun, though it doesn't feel finished. If you really like management games, this will probably feel pretty empty to you. Though if you don't regularly play management games, or want something somewhat simpler, this is for you. You may also enjoy this if you like making up stories for your characters, as there is a sort of social network generated for each character that you can kinda use to judge their emotional state.
It has several interesting mechanics, such as raiders which will stop by on their own ship, or derelict ships that will occasionally spawn. These become structures which can be salvaged or incorporated into your own ship, which can be pretty cool. The whole oxygen management thing in general is definitely my favorite part of this game. If you lose a wall of a room to a raider drill, meteors, or anything like that, your guys will be sucked out of that room, and oxygen levels will plumet. Its always fun having to quickly suit up some builders to patch a hole before everyone dies of asphyxiation.

I have been playing this game for a while now, it has grown into such a great game. The developers really shine in their skill, communication, and direction. Right now it is like an uncut diamond. You can see the potential in the game, but it might not quite be there yet. If you are looking for a finished or mostly finished game, this is not yet for you. Since I bought the game, it has been drastically improved, both functionally and with new content.
For your benefit, here is my take on a few features the game offers
Multiplayer
Sorry charlie, not yet. If you play the game, you will see why its not ready, the engine is not finished and the balance is a bit off.
AI, multiple opponents
The AI saw some improvements after the game launched to Beta. Now, they attack each other and expand more often. Additionally, every race and pirate uses stronger ship designs and upgrades their fleets as they research new tech. The early game is much more brutal, simply building 10 of the default attack design won't cut it it anymore. You'll find the most challenge in this game playing against Very Hard AI, having Total War selected, and selecting a race with a low likeability.
Research
Standard researching. No real thoughts on this, its nothing to scream about, but its not bad either. To summarize.. Three tech trees, military, economy, science. Military has weapons, ship modules, and fleet and ground attack buffs. Economy has money and diplomacy buffs and a few economic buildings. Science allows you to colonize worse conditioned planets, terraform, buff science production, and has a few buildings.
Ship Design
Its a rudimentary system currently, but it has already seen some major improvements. Currently there are 4 hull sizes available from Scout up to Capital. Your different ship parts have weights and can only be placed in certain predetermined spots.
Ships and space combat
Use shipyard planets to build ships. Then conquer the galaxy. Space combat is psuedo turn based. Each player takes a turn with his whole army and attacker goes first. You can move a ship, then move another ship, then come back to your previous ship and attack with it. I like to move all my stuff then attack with it. There is automatic combat resolving, but like most 4X games you can do much better when you control combat manually.
Random Events, Minor Races, Pirates, Espionage, Diplomacy
There is a decent amount of variety but like any game if you play enough you will see it repeat a lot. Someday they are going to add in Race specific story line events, the race backgrounds (detailed in the manual) are quite good, but that story is not yet integrated with the game. The game offers espionage and diplomacy. These features are being worked on and have seen some improvements over the last few months.
Game graphics and performance
The graphics are beautiful. The camera angles are not great yet, but you can see that your able to zoom into fine detail and it still looks good. The developers recently said on the forums that their intention is to make combat more cinematic so it feels more exciting, you can see already that they will be able to pull that off
Game sound
Some of the sound effects are much louder than others, so occasionally you will jump at some sounds (like a missile exploding or when you deliver any of the speeches). The music is deliciously good in this game, I never noticed it until the Beta launch reset my settings to default.

It’s a Sandbox, GTA style game.

The Surge is an action game, not an action RPG like the games it's usually compared to. There is much more emphasis on combat and defeating difficult enemies with limited tools, rather than in-depth character creation and long term min-maxing with builds. It seems like this game is either loved or hated for the combat, likely because it's more skill-based than Souls. I'll draw some comparisons to explain why:
Upgrades in the Surge are locked behind both region/discovery and player level together, so when progressing through areas and bosses you are restricted to whats available until that point. You can't spend tech scrap to increase your health or damage. Souls, on the other hand, allows you to improve your stats by grinding levels anytime, allowing you to grind until enemies are easier to defeat.
The few ranged attacks in The Surge must be charged by melee attacks before they can be used, so there's no possibility of cheesing levels or bosses with ranged. You have to progress by mastering the combat system.

Keeping it short and sweet, I have been enjoying The Surge. I'm a big fan of the "Soulslike" genre, and have played both the good and the bad. This one is definitely good.
"Is it a DkS clone?"
Yes and no. Combat is dangerous, you drop your collected currency upon death, and... well, that's really all that's carbon copied. Everything else has a rather unique and pleasant spin. Weight, for instance, is now handled through Core Power. If you want to wear heavy armor you need to be able to provide it with plenty of juice. You can wear lighter armor and go with plenty of powerful implants instead if you'd rather be more nimble. There are no stats, so "builds" aren't really a thing. Challenge runs are probably going to be more popular with this game instead of playing through it again with a different build.
"How's the combat?"
It feels good and the controls are tight. There are a few tutorials you can miss in the beginning area (I didn't realize I could jump out of a sprint until the third zone) so make sure to explore the controls thoroughly. Speaking of exploring, make sure to test out every new weapon type you find. There are lots of different combos that can be done by pressing light attack and heavy attack in the correct order. Some are quite vicious, and on the topic of viciousness you can gain power in combat by striking enemies to brutally execute them. It's quite pleasing to the eye! Besides choppnig off arms,, legs, and heads (you can target specific body parts in order to more effectively lop them off) cutting up your foes provides you with salvage and parts. Collect new armor sets by chopping up your enemy and learning the schematics, then build your own!
"Is it buggy?"
I've encountered one or two strange things in the game, though both happened with the first boss. Apart from that encounter I've yet to find anything game breaking or even inconveniencing.
"Is the story good?"
So far it has been. It's told through audio logs, conversations, and visual clues. I can't comment on whether or not the ending is solid, but I'm sure you can find out from other reviewers whether that's the case.
"Does it look good?"
As a lover of gritty sci-fi, I have really enjoyed seeing all of the environments and enemies. Keep in mind that a lot of the armor and weapons are tools, especially at the beginning of the game. Don't go into it expeecting to look like a space marine, since you'll end up looking more like a space construction worker. Seeing as how that fits the game's theme and setting, I think they did a great job.
Hopefully I've answered some of your questions in this review. In closing I'd say once again that I recommend this game is you're a Soulslike lover that wants a new twist on the formula. Dark Souls it ain't, and that's okay.

This game has kept me enthralled ever since I got it. This is the most appealing game concept for me and I have not been able to shake off the fact that this game is awesome. In essence, the game is what you think it might be; a resource management/survival game where you have to improve your weapons and your factory while watching out for the ravenous enemies that steadily get more powerful the more you pollute their untouched planet. (It does kinda make you feel like the bad guy, doesn't it?) Mildly interesting concept, right?
BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE!
You're allowed to intricately manage every part of the mega factory system that you built with your bare hands. (At least, until your own mechanical robot slaves build it for you, but we'll get to that later.) The point is there are thousands of ways to get resource A to factory B and then transport product C to site D so that it can be used in making science kit E. With a limitless open world, you have plenty of room, so how are you going to do it? It all seems so complicated when you first get the game, but if you keep your wits about you, you learn from every playthrough. Soon, you'll be making power armor, laser turrets, rocket launchers, slave robots, and all sorts of other technological goodies that the game has to offer. Plus, there's an awesome community that has hundreds of great ideas on organizational tips for your base.
But enough about play and plot. How good is the design?

I eventually had a fleet of cargo ships and fighter escorts that protected my convoy as it moved through dangerous trade routes. The trade system is easy to use once you get a hang of it and it can be extremely rewarding to find a trade route that you can stick too. (Hint: try the rim to the alien worlds)

I like it if there were more options for fleet organization but for a free game this is impressive enough.

Amazing game. I honestly don't know how it is free. I would easily put down anywhere from 15 to 20 dollars for this, as I really do enjoy it that much.
It's got a lot of features, and a huge variety of each at that, such as ships, ship outfittings (think engines, guns, etc) routes, planets (and other destinations), species/civilizations, missions, commodities for trading (and their local pricings), and ways of profiting (Are you more a Captain Malcolm Reynolds or more a Captain Jean-Luc Picard?).

It can be challenging at times and very detailed, but it's neat and not overwhelming either in my opinion, plus mods, so I definitely recommend you give it a shot.
Besides, it's all free. You don't have much to lose besides an hour or two at the most if you don't like it. If you do, then you got plenty of content to dive into!

I don't review much, and I typically am not an MMO fan.  To date, the only ones I've put significant time towards are DC Universe Online and Star Trek Online.  However, after logging 86.8 hours of FFXIV in a bit under 10 days, despite being a gainfully employed adult, I'd have to give this one an overwhelmingly positive review.
This is the first FF game in a long while (probably since FF7 - which I played when it originally came out), that has made me not want to tear myself away from playing.  The story/dialogue can be a little cheesy sometimes, but it's FF, it's supposed to be.
Game mechanics are fun, can be learned easily, and with the XP boost until lvl 60, it gives noobs an easy opportunity to try different classes (or all of them) without it being particularly punishing if you don't like one.  The game does a great job of drawing you in an letting you try being anything you want easily.
People that tend to lean towards soloing can have plenty of fun (I tend this direction), and as far as I've seen the community is predominantly kind and willing to teach.  You can also easily find groups (Free Companies - which are equal to Guilds, Leagues, Fleets, etc. in other MMOs) to join and they are eager to help you learn the ropes.
There's plenty to do and try in FFXIV and fun to be had.  It's consistently rated in the top MMOs for good reason.
The only negative aspect I see is that it is a subscription based model, but there's an indefinite free trial now.  So, you can experience everything up to level 35 with all of the classes before you decide if you're willing to give SE your money.

Star Lords Alpha Build - Pre-release Review
Star Lords, by Arkavi Studios and Iceberg Interactive is a deep and complex turn based 4x sci-fy strategy game. This is about the only informations you get from the get-go once you boot the game for the first time. Once you start a new game, you will be asked to select from a group of 8 original races and customise the "game board".
Once the game begins, you'll immediately take control of your chosen race and you can start using your scout ship to explore your surroundings. You also get a home planet, which will be  used as a main hub for initial development.
The game leaves a pretty good first impression, with very nice and clean graphical information. The UI is functional and simple, but can become a bit overwhelming for starters, but all in all everything is pretty intuitive. But, being this an alpha build, i must stress the importance of the creation of a structured tutorial, so players can learn and try the base mechanics before being sent into the wild.
Once the game starts building up pace, you will meet other civilizations, which you will need to either crush with military prowess or outsmart through diplomacy and espionage. Overall, the AI is pretty solid, even though other races can be tad temperamental towards your actions
The game map, even though presented in a very simplistic fashion, works very well and offers a ton of graphical variety. Planets look pretty good, and so does spacial debris and other celestial bodies, such as moons and stars.
The game still lacks a bit of clear indicative elements, such as an "it is now your turn" prompt, or some audio feedback on research completion but, as it is in alpha, hopefully these elements will be added at some point.
Veredict: There is room for a lot of improvement, specially in the fine details, but as this is just an alpha build, i will be eagerly expecting the finished product, and i am glad to be supporting it!

Although this game, as I've already played it for about 3 hours and planning on for longer, is very new, I htink it has enough potential in it to be worth checking out, the tutorials don't explain everything, but it's still in alpha, so I hope that will  be fixed in later versions

A side-project by the venerable Double Fine, Spacebase DF-9 had ambitions of being “Dwarf Fortress but in SPACE!”. It’s in space, that part they finished pretty early on. The entire everything else part, the parts that involve managing a large, complex and interrelated system of many smaller systems all working together and against each other, that part they didn’t quite finish. Much of what was promised for Spacebase DF-9 was dropped just before release (the game had been in Early Access for about a year now). The game was given a half-decent tutorial, opened up so users could modify and “finish” the game themselves, and a few meta-goals were added to give the experience a bit of structure.
So what you’re left with is something that so painfully looks like the start of something great but then never actually goes there.  You can build your base, take on space immigrants, juggle their needs and desires, fend off raiders and explore derelicts that may appear. But it all feels pointless, unless you chase the arbitrary goals the team shoved in at the last minute, like “have a base with X amount of denizens”. It’s a pity the game didn’t get more support in Early Access, as a lack of interest from consumers is why Double Fine claims to have dropped the project.

So I guess this is what happened:
- Tim Schafer goes to a handful of investors with a prototype for a game. A game that has potential, a game that has that Double Fine sense of humor we all love, and a game that will fill a void in the market that has been left open for far too long.
- The investors love it and give Tim Schafer $400,000 to make this game.
- Tim Schafer gets addicted to cocaine and hookers and completely blows (heh) all of his investors' money, but just about this time Steam early access was hitting its stride and crafty Schafer cooks up a scheme.
- Tim Schafer puts a very early, borderline-developmental build of DF9 up on steam for $25 with a link to a web page promising tons and tons of features - all with a very nebulous timetable attached.
- A few months later (and a few inconsequential updates later) Tim Schafer finally cons enough money from hard-working people to pay back his investors (and get himself into rehab). Unfortunately, Double Fine is now broke.
- Tim Schafer announces the latest development build as the final release, takes down the webpage with the planned content, and releases the source code in a futile attempt to placate his former fans.
- Tim Schafer goes off to further bankrupt Double Fine.
tl;dr,
.  This game is fundamentally broken and lacking in content.
I realize game development can be expensive, but I think it's pretty obvious from this and the Broken Age debacles that Tim Schafer isn't particularly good with money. Maybe Double Fine's next project should be an Excel spreadsheet so he can keep track of expenses.
Also, I really don't see how releasing the source code, or modding API, or whatever will possibly save this turd.  Modders are not going to want to spend time making a bad game adequate.  I think a complete rewrite of the AI should be the first thing to be done, but by the time they familiarize themselves with the code and rework the game, it'll be months from now. Months of work, just to maybe make the game playable and - best case senario - make Tim Schafer a few more bucks from sales.

Despite the hours I have played this game for, it is fair to say this game does have a lot of rough edges. The voice acting for one is especially dire.
So in typical MoW fashion you can control all manner of troops, guns and tanks as well as the inventory managment down to individual soldiers. The mpas as ever are quite large and detailed and pretty much everything is destructible. And whilst the graphics, animations and sound are all pretty decent, the game is bugged with the same issues as other games in the men of war series.
Mainly pathfinding and AI issues. So yes the enemy AI on a field gun will still wreck your tanks with out any problem, your own AI manages to miss enemy tanks even when the directtly in front of them. And yes trying to get your soldiers from A to B is like herding cats. And yes there are times when you will need to save scum like mad to achieve certain objectives.
Other frustrations include trying to build defenses and squad managment. Well bascially there is no real squad managment as things tend to go south pretty quickly leaving you with troops and odd units all over the maps. Same with defense building there is simply not enough time to ever really utilise the tools given effecttivly.
The game also suffers from some technical bugs such as campaigns that cannot be completed, or sometmes events not triggering until you reload and replay the mission a few times.
So basically if your a sucker for punishment like me and you like the MoW series, and linterested in the WW1 setting then this is worth a look. And if you buy the full deluxe version then you do at least get a lot of campaigns for the money (if they don't bug out). If your on the fence I really recommend waiting for a steam sale.
If you don't like the MoW series then this will not change your mind. It will just remind you why you hate those games in the first place.

I almost never write reviews on steam but I have to for this masterpeice of a game. The combat in this game is innovative and creative, not only that the combat directly coincides with your acquiring gear and weapons. there are no stats in this game, to respec you simply replace your gear with different gear, same with weapon.
There are 3 gear types. you have operator, your extremely light but quick set, low stability meaning you may get knocked down more than you like, it can increase your attack speed, and also it can drastically decrease not only energy spent on your drone, but stamina consumed with running or dodging or even just stamina spent in general. Personally i just finished my playthrough wearing nothing but operator sets my way through. Secondly you have sentinel, sentinel is your medium set, his has medium stability, and dependant upon set can either add to or decrease the amount of stamina consumed, i never found a sentinel set that decreased or increased attack speed either, but the defense was higher than that of operator. So think of Sentinel as your jack of trades middle ground sets. Lastly you have goliath, and it is properly named. These behemoth sets can drastically decrease attack speed, and drastically increase stamina consumption in all areas and energy consumption on drones drastically once more. With all these cons youd think it was worthless but goliath sets turn you into a hulking tank, so if your plastyle is the slow smashy type. go for it.
Next up we have weapons. single rigged is a one handed weapon attached at the wrist, it has low attack speed, high impact (the higher your impact, the more likely you are to stagger and knock down enemies) and amazing damage, single rigged weapons from my playthrough showed to have the highest damage of any weapon in the game, maxing at 120. One handed weapons are swords and the occasional mace you find, medium attack speed, medium impact, medium everything pretty much, imo the damage isnt all to great but its much better than our next sad contestant, twin-rigged. Twin rigged is 2 blades attached to both wrists, with very low impact and exceedingly low damage (highest i saw was a mark 4 with 38 damage), it boasts extremely high attack speeds  but with these your playstyle will become excessively hit and run.
After that we have staves, staves have some of the weirdest movesets in the game, they boast medium impact, not too great damage. next up, we have heavy duty, our last in the weapons category. In an odd twist of events, heavy duty weapons boast the slowest attack speed, but the second highest damage, under single-rigged. The highest damage heavy duty i found was 79 damage with an end game weapon. These weapons boost some of the highest impact tho, and knock down enemies quite frequently. Weapons also have certain energy gain levels which increase energy attained from attacking, in order from highest average to lowest average EN gain we have: Heavy Duty, Single Rigged, staves, one handed, and twin rigged. Also with weapons there is profiency scaling, as you use a weapon type more you become more profiecient with it, i imagine this increases damage done but its effect was never obvious. again in order of highest to lowest average gain of Prof scaling we have: Twin rigged, Single rigged, one handed, staves, and then heavy duty.
As you can see this game has quite alot of depth to it and im not really done explaining its most base parts, instead of stats you have implants, these implants almost always stack and increase stamina, energy, hp, healing potions, regen potions, and so much more, there are so many implants with different effects it would take we 30 minutes to explain them all. But to use these implants you need to upgrade your power score. your power core is your level, the higher level it is, the better gear and implants you can use. the only thing that doesnt use core power is your weapon.
To acquire all this gear and weaponry you have to make use of the games combat mechanic of dismemberment. If you see an enemy with something you want, target that limb, beat the ever loving ♥♥♥♥ out of it, and then when you have the energy if hes still alive, cut it the ♥♥♥♥ off. Its satisfying as hell. Your currency is tech scrap, if youre afraid of losing it you can store it at this games version of the bonfire, ops, which has a medbay and gear assembler.
The story may be very paced out, but it will always be at the back of your mind, wondering whats going to happen next as you journey through the Zombie(ish) infested halls of the CREO orginization.
You play as Warren, a cripple who saw an advertisement and decided to join CREO to help make the world a better place, but when he enters the surgical bay to get his RIG installed, the sedative doesn't work, and Warren is subject to machines drilling holes into his bones and even his skull, slicing his flesh as it welds peices of machinery into him. The pain is so intense that Warren passes out and you wake up in a junkyard, no idea what has happened. A drone dragging you by the leg you pick up a broken piston and destroy it. You make your way through the junkyard as best you can, when you find an Ops, a women is there on a holocommunicator, you find out her name is Sally, she will be as close to a guide as you get in this game.
And that my dear friend is where the journey begins. If you have been pondering getting this game, do it. Its well worth it.

Disclaimer: This review is from someone who played the game STARTING at the most recent version, NOT in the incomplete Early Access version.
As its title suggests, Spacebase DF-9 is essentially a cross between Dwarf Fortress and Star Trek Deep Space 9. Compared to other games of the colony planning genre, the complexity of game content is fairly low, but the visuals are far more detailed and approachable; What I mean is, where in other games you may be struggling to remember what that static @ on the map represents, or which one of your little colored peg people was a particular character, in Spacebases you can tell at a glance what job an individual crew member is assigned to, what they're doing, and even how they're feeling, with an exaggerated moping walk when they're upset or a bounce in their step and head held high when they're happy.
The space setting gives way to elements you won't find in most other colony planning games, such as oxygen management, exploring potentially dangerous derelict vessels, asteroid storms and chest-bursting parasite monsters, but common themes remain such as the importance of high morale and dealing with tantrum-throwing or fighting crew if that morale drops,  dealing with disease outbreaks and fighting off (or capturing and reforming) invading forces.
Despite the amount or complexity of content not being that deep, I've still found fourty-plus hours so far of thorough enjoyment through catastrophic failures and the desire to "build it better the next time", and much like in a Roguelike, I manage to do better, and make a spacebase survive longer, than each previous attempt.
Decide for yourself what price you're willing to pay for a simplistic colony planner, but if you're a fan of them and love anything space-related, I think you'll enjoy this game.

You might think "Wow, a mix between dead space and Dark Souls? What could go wrong!" The answer is: So much. So damn much can go wrong.
First off, its not as atmospheric as dead space or dark souls. By far not. The Combat is much worse than in Dark Souls (Cant compare to Dead Space since its not ranged), you get thrown around by your attacks which are slower than in dark souls (By that i mean the time you cant do anything is much higher, not really the attack itself), the enemies attacking stagger you so hard you easily die by being hit once (Oh, a bullet that does 5% of my health. It hit me so all others do an i cant act for 5 seconds, what a great idea!) and the dumbest thing ive seen so far: Finishing moves which take the control off the player move around so much you get just thrown down some edge by chance. You might think itd be fair to say "Well, if he cant react or move we dont want some unforseeable animation/move to let him jump down a cliff" but nope. Absolutely will happen and kill you.
The Voice actors also seem way off. Never seen so many "Hm, whats going on around here, who cares. Just the roboapocalypse, nothing special" people walking around except in college films. The protagonist is also like "Hm, just got drilled in my Flesh and Bones while being alive and wake up in a desert scrapyard with robots attacking me. Good thing i got all these flashy super moves i learned while being crippled to kill them. Ah, a woman from a communicator talks to me. Lets ask whats happening here and then have no emotions for the rest of the game."
But id forgive all that (Except that falling off a cliff). Really, i could take that, have seen much worse. But what really makes the game feel bad is that everything seems too unfair. Its not like in DS that its hard challenge but you can overcome that and feel great, its more like "rng made me lose there, lets try as long as it takes so i do win" and it doesnt feel good at all. Just like you won a dice roll in quite some places.

Borderlands 2 is a very unique game, it's genre would be best described as a First-Person Shooter Role Playing Game (FPS RPG).
It has a lovely balance between Story, Quest Hunting, Loot-hoarding and Comedy. Yes, that's right! Comedy in an RPG game.. we must be on heaven.
The game's story line is a vague follow up of the games predecessor, Borderlands. It is set on the fictional planet of Pandora, a savage world filled with foreign and psychotic creatures who want nothing more than you to fail in whatever it is you are doing, hostile is the lightest term for how the inhabitants of Pandora act.
, a vault hunter, are tasked with discovering a mighty vault filled with treasures beyond your wildest dreams. Be warned though! You are not the only one who seaks what this vault contains; a villainous man by the name of Jack, along with the corrupt company Hyperion, has come to claim the vault for himself.
When you begin your journey into the Borderlands, right of the bat you have a character selection screen; it is always good to have a variety of play styles and customisation options available to you. The characters available (in the base game) are:
All of these characters have upgrade paths to follow, all providing buffs to your character of choice; the route you follow is progressive but completely up to you! Do you fancy making your Zer0 a melee god? Turn the game into a punching party? Then feel free! That is completely possible.
Something to note in all of the Borderlands 2 series, is that when the story mode ends and the almost never-ending list of side quests have been completed; there is a loot system. You can go and farm for the rarest and most powerful gear in the game, collect the coolest guns or kill the hardest bosses! The fun doesn't end with the story. To some however, this may not appear as fun. The grinding for loot and farming of bosses may not appeal to you. That is fine, the game as plenty to offer within the standard playthrough of the game and even more so with the several expansions packs available.
To conclude, I am of the opinion that Borderlands 2 is a fantastic game, it has a very expansive system of gameplay that can fulfill the needs of casual gamers and RPG enthusiasts alike! I for one would put the series of Borderlands at the top of my games list; with Borderlands 2 being number 1.

Pros:
- You only need one character, all Jobs ( classes) and professions (gathering and crafting) can be done on the same character.
- Jobs are all relatively easy to play at first, but later get more complex. Incorperating mechanics such as flanking an enemy to get optimal damage output.
- The combat system is pretty straight forward, running off of a proc based system for most classes.
- The music is wonderfully done, everytime combat starts i get a small nastolgic blast.
- The expansions are extremely well done, the recent one Storm blood making extremely nice quality of life changes.
- The graphics are pretty good, though bare in mind this was originally designed with PS# support in mind. though Storm Blood did not end up with that restriction.
- There is two diferent subscription types, one that allows for only one character per world, the other allowing up too eight.
Cons:
- The base game is filled with cutscenes in which there is no voice acting, unless extremely improtant plot is happening. This isn't a huge negative but it may annoy some people.
- Based on what server you are you will either get WoW levels of toxicity, or a super friendly community.
-If you are coming into the game now, prepare for a semi-long slog through content that is fairly old and less populated.
- DPS is the most common type of class within the game, so prepare for some lengthy wait times, though tanks and healers almost always instant que.
- professions in this gameare a pain too grind up, due to the fact you need to have both gathering classes leveled. If you only have one well prepare for a good long struggle.
- The player market is full of greedy people and should be avoided until "end game". Most anything you need such as new armour or potions can be bought at merchants now.
Now other then these pros, and Cons, i would like to say the game is fantastic. After 450+ hours i can safely say i'm still invested in the game. Especially since they are constently updating the game with either new content for the expansion, or game fixes quite frequently. If you are a Final Fantasy fan and love a game that pays homage to the series with easter eggs galour, as well as an MMO fan who enjoys great story with good combat. Then this is most certanly the game for you, and i would reccomend it 100%. Mabe you might run into me on sargatanas, keep an eye out for Arngrims Eichenwolf.

-Intro: I have absolutely nothing but good things to say about this game. From the graphics to the gameplay, this game just keeps me wanting more and I'm kind of sad the game couldn't be longer (~18 hours including DLC). Since I speak Cantonese, one of the best things about this game is that it's FILLED with Cantonese profanities every five seconds and it's honestly the BEST. THING. EVER.
-Plot: Without spoiling anything, you play the game as Wei Shen, an undercover cop working within the a Hong Kong triad and throughout the game you complete missions for both the police and triads, and you can level up to earn upgrades. The story isn't "WOW" like NieR: Automata, but it's still enough to make you wonder what happens next.
-Gameplay: The main combat of the game is hand-to-hand, and it revolves around a system built on flashy martial arts combos. There are missions where you need to pick up a gun and take down enemies, and it's very similar to Tom Clancy's The Division where you can duck behind covers and such. There are side missions where you have to race in sports cars & run from cops, and it honestly feels like I'm playing Need For Speed at some point. The driving controls are pretty smooth, and it's pretty intuitive.
-Graphics: The graphics are ABSOLUTELY STUNNING. There are times where I would have my character walk a long distance to the missions just so I can absorb the scenery. Overall, it's such a scenic game that you will find yourself just walking around doing nothing but taking a look at your surroundings.
-If I had to nitpick, I'd say the gameplay does feel a bit repetitive at times but it takes place in different parts of town so each mission feels different. Also, the game only has one difficulty and it's not really all that challenging.
Rating: 9.0/10

Legend of Grimrock is a throwback to the core of the RPG genre. Stat based dungeon crawling. No mouse twitching skills required. No pseudo-choices that have no gameplay effects. No dialog pretending to be grey.
This is pure RPG gameplay. You create your party and fight through a dungeon of monsters finding new equipment and leveling up their skills and stats as you go along.
Despite the fairly oldschool grid based gameplay it is a pretty game, with good sounds, great exploration, hard to find secrets and frustrating puzzles. The combat might seem simple from the outside but movement will play a major part in the harder battles and particularly on the harder difficulties.
If there was something bad to say about this game it was a relatively short main campaign but the addition of Steam Workshop fixed that.
A great buy.

Burstfire is a lower bugdet knock-off of Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege.  The game mimics just about every feature of R6 Siege with a few things of their own like improved class abilities, but offers no single player.
I like tactical styled games so I purchased three copies of this game for my sons and I to play while we wait for R6 Siege to release. Yes I have played the Alphas for R6 Siege and subsequently pre-ordered the game even though it was glitch infested, but then I own all of the Tom Clancy R6 & Ghost Recon games.
This game has potential but needs a lot of work, a lot.  I believe that if Nacho Games developes a high quality indie game, say like Hawking, the potential is there for a highly popular shooter at an affordable price with the possibility of DLC in the future for maps, weapons, and skins.  Another possibility is community support which would be awesome. This game could be very popular if successful.
My experiance however was disappointing.  The match making system combined with a poor reputation of the publisher, Free Reign Entertainment, and adverse opinions of Burstfire being a R6 Ripoff has killed this game.  The game seriously needs to be able to start rounds with 2v2, not making players wait for 30 plus minutes for a 5v5.  For the two hours I have in this game, 92% of that was spent waiting in ques to see the number of players rise and fall but rarely hitting the required 10 players to start a round. I played three 2-3 min rounds in a two hour period.  I waited for just over two weeks logging in regularly to check ques hoping for a game but that just never happened so I got a refund on my $45 for my purchase of three games.
Fast paced tactical combat (R6 clone)
Destructible environment
Open class system (Awesome)
Affordable for most PC gamers (high potential)
Horrible match making system (must have 10 player to start a round)
No BOTs (prohibits the ability to play this alone when you cannot find players online)
Glitchy gameplay (can be expected from an incomplete game in an alpha state)
Poorly optimised with limited graphics options (no sli support, FoV distorts your view as if your looking out of a fish bowl, and drops in fps)
The graphics (engine seems dated)
Hackers (didn't see any myself in my three rounds, but I did in videos on YouTube)
I would like to see this game succeed but for the moment I cannot recommend this game.  Before I purchase this title again and update this review to a recommend status, I would need to see that the match making system was redesigned to include bots so the game is actually playable at any time, server support, and either some graphical improvements or an engine overhaul.

Hello gents, I have just completed all achievements at New Game +++ at Core Level 150 using Full Lynx and Gestalt, focusing on Health Implants. Sorry this review is not exciting, it is informative with some focus on mechanics.
First off, lets address the main complaints of the negative reviews.
(I'd like to just go ahead and note that if anyone says this game is bad because it's too hard, then they are probably just trash, you know the type to be at the bottom of the K/D page)
[Enemies are OP with Super Armor and you have to resort to dash attacks with High Impact weapons]
-The strongest weapon in the game is a dual-rigged medium impact weapon that is based of speed, not impact.
-If you are just dash attacking once and then jumping out, you don't understand the targeting/impact mechanics of the game, this only becomes a game where you can dash-attack-combo chain in one fell swoop and completely obliterate the enemy once you have the best and proper gear. Expect to use your brain and reflexes otherwise.
-Whoever made up the word "Super Armor" is probably referring to high-stability armor, as enemies in the game wear the same armor that is available to you and vice-versa. So, how can you complain, you can wear "Super Armor" too.
[The Levels are so repetitive and there's no directions on where to go]
-There are fu**ing signs, there are literally fu**ing signs that tell you where things are. If the game brings you full circle back to the start of somewhere it is telling you one of two things "Here, have a free shortcut back the Medlab/Ops, OR something has now opened up that wasn't before. They aren't just messing with you.
-Every single area in the game uses different textures and has a different look. I'm so confused by this complaint. I'm convinced that this is another complaint by people who die a lot. Yes, my friend, you truly are seeing the same thing over and over again.
I just wanted to get that out of the way because I almost didn't get this game based of negative reviews. By all means, if you know you're not a decent gamer, the negative reviews will be true to your heart.
The game for me personally was interesting, I found all the audio files and the people you meet to be rewarding in their own way. The story itself wasn't phenomenal, but a few of the character developments (not including you) were quite exceptional. I actually thought some of the side-stories were more interesting than the main. If you like the fall of humanity stuff, you'll probably enjoy the story of this game.
Gameplay was legit, the enemies have enough move variation that when you know exactly how to kill something, they can surprise you every now and then. Every enemy type needs to be approached in a different way, but nonetheless if you know their weakness, they'll just be scrap for you to collect. If you feel like they don't have a weakness, keep looking, each enemy does. Ex. Some enemies, if you hit them in the leg, they will ALWAYS buckle. There is something that I have noticed though. There seems to be some sort of defensive fill-up bar that may be running in the background. If you try to land a secondary full-combo , they will almost always attack during your combo. To reset this all you need to do is allow them to 2-3 seconds after you finish your first full-combo.
Sound and music was aight.
Graphics are legit, up to date stuff.
Is it worth the price tag? The price is on the higher-end for the content, but they're not ripping you off by any means. They didn't make it $60 for a reason.

For all those people who love old school Role Playing Games and those who feel that the genre needs to be a bit faster paced this is that game for you. Cthulhu Saves the World is a fantastic indie RPG, that last about 10 hours, where you play of the lord of insanity right when he loses all of his powers. In order to get them back he needs to become a hero and save the world (several times). Along the way he meets many characters that are fun to play with and add depth to conversations. Gameplay is turn based combat in first person with text representing up to 4 characters that you can have in combat. Each character can focus on strength or magic so you can customize their stats with gear and 2 different choices when they level. They can also learn or enhance spells depending on the choices and all characters gain experience regardless of if they were in combat or not. One of my favorite features that i wish were in more RPG's is the limited encounter system. In each area you can only have to fight so many enemies until the game decides you have fought enough, you can still fight enemies by selecting fight but this is not required. The humor in Cthulhu is some of the best in video games. There are references everywhere and the way the characters interact is just so great. There is no reason not to get this game. It cost less than lunch and comes with a bonus RPG that is almost as good. Get this game if you want a fun, funny and fast RPG. P.S. 4 new game modes after you beat the game.
Who wouldn't want to save the world, just to destroy it later with insanity and the epic awesomness of Cthulhu? No one! That's who! Best cheap game I've ever played.

First things first: this game is great. It has been one of the most fun experiences I've ever had as a gamer. Which is why I’m more than happy about being able to switch my review from a negative to a positive. Previously, I felt I had to give the game a thumbs down (despite loving it to death) due to the way Square Enix handled their price changes in Brazil and Russia (that is, without any sort of forewarning). At long last, both Brazilian and Russian players got an official response in regards to the so called price adjustment. Furthermore, the prices will be reverted back to what it used to be on August 16th (during an upcoming maintenance), and the new rate they wish to introduce will return 60 days after the change, as per Square Enix’s warning. Although I remain sad that the price will be changed, and that I still think it’s an abusive price for those 2 regions, as I said on my previous review, they are within their rights to do so. Now they are doing the price change as a company should at the very least, giving their customers a heads up so they can adjust to the situation. And just as I expressed my frustration against Square Enix before for what I felt was a disrespect towards their customer base, I have to commend them for going back and doing something to address the issue (fair is fair, after all). So, there we go, the game remains as awesome as ever and hopefully Square Enix will keep this little episode in mind if they ever decide to make another big change like this again.
As it stands, I’m more than glad to give this game a full recommendation once more for anyone interested in a fun MMORPG. Just keep in mind it will be quite expensive depending on your region (I believe you’ll get your money’s worth, though).

Previously I would've recommended it, until the developer announced that they were dropping the game so soon.
I was a backer since the start. Although it had been left in a playable state, with the code made open source for the community to develop on, it's still a kick in the nuts that the game is left at only a fraction of what they promised Spacebase DF-9 was going to be.
Everything works you see, but there are issues:
-----
> AI are still dumb at times.
I've seen people stand in a corridor when a meteor shower hits the base, or people outside the airlock suffocate because they're waiting in line and their suits run out of oxygen.
> Limited gameplay.
Once you've built a self-sustaining base thats it. You're done. No more challenge outside of the occassional random events or purposely putting yourself into a situation.
> Limited reply value.
You get one save file and one base, unless you manually switch them out in folders. Every replay is building the same base again until you come up with an efficient design that always works - its more of a time waster.
> No more official development.
You'll recieve support, but any further addons are now in the hands of the community.
-----
If you're looking for a time waster with simple space-base building mechanics, then maybe this is for you. Its quick to load, with enough advanced features to keep things interesting while you don't have to micro-manage everything.
If you're looking for a game to compare to Space Engineers however? I'd suggest saving that money. You'll likely make one base or two, learn the mechanics, develop a strategy to quickly 'win' everytime and then get bored quickly.
Its a damn shame this game didn't make enough money so was dropped.

For me, this game is truly a timless experience. Playing as an immigration officer along the Grestin border of Arstotska, you job is to check passports and other papers to make sure they are legal to enter. A game with 20 endings that vary on the choices you made through 25 days on the Grestin border.

What starts as a simple game of border guard drone quickly becomes a lot more intriguing as you find yourself caught up in small dramas, corrupt government officials, and an even bigger conspiracy involving the Underground. You're torn between doing what's right and doing what will hopefully shield your family from the 'justice' of your own government.It's like you're working the Berlin Wall in the 80's. Google is your friend.
Simple visuals, and smart controls compliment the story of Papers, Please. The learning curve works with you, as every day on the job offers a new challenge, and yes, there are achievements for you completionists out there.
The feeling of pressure mounting as you work against the clock to do your job AND make choices that will affect the outcome of your game (and there are over a dozen different possible endings) is so real you may find yourself having to step away and weigh your decisions.
I highly recommend this game. Totally worth the price (bonus if it's on sale).
The clock is ticking. They're watching your every move. What will you do next?
Glory to Arstotzka.

TLDR: Papers, Please is a fantastic way to spend a free hour or two here and there, it's one of my all-time favorites and worth the price whether it's on sale or not.
Pros:
+Great atmosphere
+Challenging decisions that really impact the ending
+Interesting mini-puzzles and events
Cons:
-Some nitpicky details
Papers, Please is one of my favorite games to date. Upon first starting the game, you're greeted with a booming Arstotzkan theme and immediately dumped into the thick atmosphere of the game. It's a fairly rare occasion for a game with such a simple and pixelated graphic style to be as immersive as this one, which really puts you into your role as a winner of the labor lottery.
Along the way, you come accross a ton of characters, many of which forcing you to make big decisions that could impact the life of you or the family you're working to care for. What's worse is that most times you won't see the effect of your decision until days after, leaving you tense and concerned that soon enough, your world will crumble around you.
Some of the characters that come by will make you think harder than others, some giving you challenges on a surface level, whilst others force you to decipher more thoroughly, meaning you have to keep up with whatever puzzle is presented, and in the meantime maintain the efforts of your job.
The only con I would mark for this game is the small details that you can get caught up on, like making sure that people have the correct issuing cities and the like.
Overall, I'd rate this game a 9/10 and definitely recommend it to anybody who's interested.

Do not underestimate this game: it is tough. Even on easy, the puzzles become daunting, the monsters brutal, and your party's resources frighteningly scarce. It's a no-joke type situation, and a person would do well to get into this with the mindset of committing to a hardcore adventure.
Nonetheless, I find the challenge a good thing. It's refreshing to have to think in a video game again and quite rewarding when you manage to proceed to another floor. You can spend a huge amount of time playing this game too--plenty of levels, lots of achievements, tons of brain teasing puzzles, plenty of weapons and gear to scavenge and disburse amongst your characters. While not for the faint of heart, this game gets my thumbs-up.

I recently posted a review about just how terrible this game was. About how enemies are faster than you in every regard, and that weapons are slow. However, given that I don't like giving up on games, I tried again, on a new character, with a different load out. (Lynx rather than Rhino. Light vs Heavy). I also used a medium speed weapon rather than the slow/very slow weapons I was using.
Holy hell what a difference. I'm making way more progress and much faster than before. On my last character I was only approaching Core level 35 when I was on my way to the 3rd boss. I'm not even at the first boss yet and I'm core level 36 with full lynx armor and weapon. The weapon damage is night and day and while I'd still like to build a tank like character with Heavy armor/weapon, it doesn't seem possible until later in the game when you have at LEAST 3 stamina boosters because of how much stamina you use with one swing of a heavy weapon.
Now that I'm decked out in light gear and a quick weapon, this game plays very much like Bloodborne and I feel right at home. Enemies are nothing now. I went into this game the same I did with Dark Souls. Heavy armor and the biggest weapon I can find from the word "go". That was my first mistake. My 2nd was not leveling enough. I didn't realize just how much the stamina and HP boosters scale from your core level. Which is why I mentioned just how little HP/stamina the boosters gave. My level was too low Especially for where I was in the game.
Lastly, I deleted that last review and re-posted this one to change my recommendation to "yes" but with a caveat. I wouldn't buy this game again for full price $50. As one of the comments on my old review mentioned, the enemy variety is lacking and there are only 5 bosses. If you can get this game for $15 or less, go for it.
Overall my biggest mistake was going heavy/heavy from the beginning and the game seems to be more punishing for those who do that. Do yourself a favor and save the headache. Go light in the beginning and farm a little to prepare.

This is an absolutely outstanding game and after reading a lot of the reviews it seems that the negative reviews are based more around peoples inability rather than the game itself. So I will go into more detail if possible by giveing each section a score out of 10.
PROS!
-Performence
It is astonishingly good. I am runningt he game at over 100fps 1440p constantly with no drops below at all. This is on the highest possible settings and on an average computer (i5 and a 980ti). 9/10
-Graphics
They are beautiful. The world is fantastic to look at, and the characters are very well detailed. There are a few low res textures here and there but they tend to be off the beaten path so do not cause any isses. Enemies are detailed and have a nice amount of variety in looks. 9/10
-Armor
The exo suits are awesome. There is a huge variet in them and all of them have lots of detail. They also provide set bonus' which does help but if you want to mix and match you are more than able to with not much of a drawback. 8/10
-Weapons
There are several types of weapons and they all feel and perform differently, but all weapons within that catagory tend to be the same with some changes but I will get into that later. They look brilliant though, all of them look like the killing machines they are meant to be and have nice effects etc. 6/10
-Combat
Here is the big one for most people. I personally love it, if you learn how to use it you will be a monster in no time. There is a learning curve to it that will punnish spammers and people that do not pay attention to stats and enemies abilities. The 'Impact' stat is pretty self explanatory. The more you have the more you stagger so the more hits you can get in and the more damage you can do. Or in the case of weapons with low impact you can get lots of fast hits in and then move away.
It is pretty standard RPG stuff to be honest. On a side note if you got on with the Lord of the Fallen combat (like me) you will fall right into your groove with this game and not have many issues at all. Overall I would say the combat is absolutely flawless, if you learn how the game plays and what abilites to use in the situation you will get on with it very well. It rewards people that think about that sort of thing instead of spamming away. 10/10.
-Leveling
You level up in the same way as most games of this genre by collecting 'souls' or in this case scrap. You take that to a medbay where you can invest it into your suits core to increase its power. The result is a higher core level, this allows you to equip 'Implants' these are things like more HP/Stamina/Energy and your healing items and so on. Also your armor pieces have energy requirements so the better the armor the more you will need. This actually works incredibly well, especially with the ability to bank your scrap so you can acess it later. 8/10
-Looting Mechanic
I am a huge fan of this. Enemies have 6 spots on them you can manually target. 2 arms 2 legs chest and head. If there is a piece of armor you are after and you see a guy wearing it, beat the snot out of that body part and rip it off him. Theres a weapon you want and you see a guy wielding that badboy? Cut that guys arm off and its yours! You get the schematic for the armor and then you can make it at a workshop. All weapons and armor are upgradeable and each NG cycle you go through their level cap is raised by 5. Its simple enough to work out and execute. 9/10
CONS
I honestly dont think there are any of real note aside from the few I will mention now.
-NG+ onwards
After beating the game you go straight into NG+ and as you probably know the game begins again. All your armor and weapons can be increased by 5 more levels, you have more slots for Implants avilable and you earn more scrap. I personally found NG+, NG++ and NG+++ to be an absolute cakewalk. On my first playthrough I was smashed about constantly and I loved it. But from then on the game was too easy, aside from a few extra enemies everything is in exactly the same spot and behave the exact same way. Yeah they hit harder but at this point you have more HP and damage than they can cope with and you destroy them in 2 hits up until maybe 2/3 of the way through then its 3 shots for the rest of the game. Sadly this suffers with Lords of the Fallen syndrome where after NG+ you may as well start a new character since you get nothing out of it. 4/10
-Content is a little lacking
It is not a long game, my first playthrough where I explored every single nook and cranny took me about 40 hours. after that I did a dew NG+ cycles and added about another 20 hours and at that point I had every item in the game and all the achievements. It left me with a little bit of disapointment that I didnt have more to do. I wanted to keep tearing peoples limbs off because I liked their shiny armor. Hopefully there will be some DLC that adds more but thats not relevant at the moment. 5/10
-Story/Voice acting
I put these together since they ggo hand in hand really. Both are a bit 'meh'. The story is a cool idea has some great cutscenes but it is pretty thin. If you listen to every audio log then you get a better lay of the land but its pretty generic to be honest. The voice acting just adds to this since it feels pretty wooden and rushed, but since there isnt much of it then it isnt the end of the world. The main characters voice actor is pretty good though. 6/10
This game is great, if you ingnore the Dark Souls fanboys that hate the combat because they cant spam with their Carthas Curved swords or poke with their Estocs then you will see that this games combat is a masterpiece. The whole game from start to finish made me smile with the grusome fighting and the incredibly satisfying gameplay.
If you are looking for 50-60 hours of violence and feeling like a hero then this is the game for you. Overall I would give it a 9/10.

Previously, I felt I had to give the game a thumbs down (despite loving it to death) due to the way Square Enix handled their price changes in Brazil and Russia (that is, without any sort of forewarning). At long last, both Brazilian and Russian players got an official response in regards to the so called price adjustment. Furthermore, the prices will be reverted back to what it used to be on August 16th (during an upcoming maintenance), and the new rate they wish to introduce will return 60 days after the change, as per Square Enix’s warning. Although I remain sad that the price will be changed, and that I still think it’s an abusive price for those 2 regions, as I said on my previous review, they are within their rights to do so. Now they are doing the price change as a company should at the very least, giving their customers a heads up so they can adjust to the situation. And just as I expressed my frustration against Square Enix before for what I felt was a disrespect towards their customer base, I have to commend them for going back and doing something to address the issue (fair is fair, after all). So, there we go, the game remains as awesome as ever and hopefully Square Enix will keep this little episode in mind if they ever decide to make another big change like this again.
As it stands, I’m more than glad to give this game a full recommendation once more for anyone interested in a fun MMORPG. Just keep in mind it will be quite expensive depending on your region (I believe you’ll get your money’s worth, though).

Transistor is a combination of RTS, third-person sci-fi RPG and really superb character class/build in a linear, hand-crafted world. Don't let the linearity of the game fool you, though.
I'd really liken this to a next-gen Legend of Zelda game, with interesting opponents, the ability to chain and modify abilities in some really intriguing ways, and an incredibly rewarding combat system with well thought out penalties for death which change how you fight, but aren't draconic.
If I stopped there, I would be doing this game a disservice. The soundtrack is nothing short of a work of art in and of itself. I've ordered it on vinyl just because it's one of the most moving and well-made soundtracks in gaming I've experienced in the last several years, and the songs transcend the game experience. For example, yes, The Witcher 3 is an amazing OST, but it wouldn't really feel right playing it for guests. This OST, however, engenders conversation and makes for an amazing background to a night of drinks, preparing a great meal, or just casual conversation.
The storyline also hit me in the feels more than any game I've encountered in recent memory, with the exception of Life Is Strange. It's moving, there's intrigue and well-paced narration, and all in all, better entertainment value than most full-length movies being produced nowadays.
This is on the list of games I truly love, and will probably end up being a game I play for decades to come.

TLDR: Papers, Please is a fantastic way to spend a free hour or two here and there, it's one of my all-time favorites and worth the price whether it's on sale or not.
Pros:
+Great atmosphere
+Challenging decisions that really impact the ending
+Interesting mini-puzzles and events
Cons:
-Some nitpicky details
Papers, Please is one of my favorite games to date. Upon first starting the game, you're greeted with a booming Arstotzkan theme and immediately dumped into the thick atmosphere of the game. It's a fairly rare occasion for a game with such a simple and pixelated graphic style to be as immersive as this one, which really puts you into your role as a winner of the labor lottery.
Along the way, you come accross a ton of characters, many of which forcing you to make big decisions that could impact the life of you or the family you're working to care for. What's worse is that most times you won't see the effect of your decision until days after, leaving you tense and concerned that soon enough, your world will crumble around you.
Some of the characters that come by will make you think harder than others, some giving you challenges on a surface level, whilst others force you to decipher more thoroughly, meaning you have to keep up with whatever puzzle is presented, and in the meantime maintain the efforts of your job.
The only con I would mark for this game is the small details that you can get caught up on, like making sure that people have the correct issuing cities and the like.
Overall, I'd rate this game a 9/10 and definitely recommend it to anybody who's interested.
